result.message: Reviewed the round-2 selu_ candidate (subject 8d098b0…) against the frozen selu_ definition/oracle/workloads and the optimize measurements. The math is the torch SELU default (scale 1.0507009873554805, alpha 1.6732632423543772, fp32 compute with cast-back to the input dtype), run(A) mutates and returns the same tensor as the Definition declares (mutates [A], out alias of A), no torch/torch.ops fallback is used for computation, and there is no host synchronization. All 24 correctness workloads exercised the raw pointer-bound launch path (shapes 0/1/1025/7x9) and passed with 0.0 error. Findings are the host-path machinery introduced in round 2: the launch cache key and the process-global cached device omit the device (a regression from round 1, which keyed on A.device.index), the object-identity fast path trusts that the tensor object's storage/numel/dtype never change between calls, the caches grow without bound and keep tensors alive, the raw launcher ABI is private and never runtime-validated, the strided kernel truncates to 8 dims, and the misaligned fallback branch is unreachable in the evaluation (the allocator is >=512B aligned, so ptr & 15 == 0 always holds). Measurement note: the supplied final_verification records geo_mean 0.9276 (<1.0) versus the search best 1.0016, with the nine launch-bound workloads rising from 8.96-10.4us to 11.3-14.0us while the reference only rose ~13-15%, so the round-2 host-side win did not reproduce. Code findings are advisory for later epochs; none of the supplied Preflight/correctness gates is duplicated here.
